# Disposable conventional lifecycle fixture

This factory embeds the staged native adapter and consumes its cached projections in process. It is not selected package membership, the installed footer factory, or a public usage event API. The selected Node backend and its production dependency behavior are unchanged.

Use only a disposable source copy and private HOME, PIG_HOME, agent, cache and temporary roots. A coordinator must supply temporary module replacements for the status and nativeusage source modules. No authored module contains a machine path. Let the frozen reviewed host stage its matching SDK in the disposable root: pointing the source loader directly at the read-only reviewed SDK makes it try to acquire that root's transaction lock.

Actual host runs require an environment allowlist, private network/PID/mount namespaces, consuming process waits and resource receipts. `--offline` is not an egress boundary. The only permitted IP connections are to the listener recorded by this factory. Its TLS trust root is local; logical official DeepSeek and OpenRouter destinations are mapped only to that listener. No live credentials, provider services, billing or session history are inputs.

Start the source factory under the frozen host in RPC mode with synthetic `openrouter/fixture` and `deepseek/fixture` models. The coordinator supplies `NA_OUTPUT` inside its owned writable root and records handled command dispositions. Wait for the initial cached quota projection, then exercise these registered controls:

1. Create `hold` in that root; select `deepseek/fixture` with `/lifecycle-model deepseek/fixture` and wait for the held HTTPS receipt.
2. Invoke `/lifecycle-config`; verify the old request is cancelled before the successor can publish. Remove `hold` so the new owner can complete.
3. Invoke `/lifecycle-close`. The fixture creates `hold`, selects `openrouter/fixture` through the awaited host context, and waits on its bounded held-request channel before recording `closing-held` and calling Close. `/lifecycle-close` drains the emitter and admitted listeners before acknowledging its join. Independent acceptance assertions check the real HTTPS cancellation and cached feed after this boundary.
4. In a separate run, use `/lifecycle-reload` while HTTPS is held. It invokes the SDK reload operation, not an unregistered raw command. The old factory drains and closes its server before its replacement becomes ready.
5. Close RPC input during an active owner to exercise ordinary shutdown. Collect process, connection and resource receipts before declaring cleanup complete.

`lifecycle.jsonl` contains only synthetic request hosts, cached quota projections, fixed failure reasons and lifecycle receipts. It never records authentication snapshots or arbitrary provider error bodies. Independent seam acceptance assertions belong to the evidence phase; this factory is the real adapter integration fixture, not their oracle.

## Extended owned-lifecycle qualification

`python3 scripts/check-native-usage.py --scenario qualification` reuses the same reviewed sandbox and synthetic TLS listener. `node --test probes/native-usage/lifecycle.test.mjs` independently asserts both the original frozen sequence and this extended scenario. The original five assertions are unchanged.

The extended run uses awaited SDK commands to rotate a synthetic registered provider, change a same-ID model's configuration, call `Collector.Refresh` through the existing fixture SDK adapter, remove a discovered Fireworks target, and fence a late successful body across settings replacement. Its body barrier buffers an actual TLS response and deliberately delivers it after the mutation; it does not implement collector fencing. It is not proof of live-provider behavior or the installed footer.

The runtime portion uses the real five-minute expiry, real failure cadence, active session replacement, reload and active-request RPC EOF. No accelerated production timer or test-only product API is used. Phase receipts delimit stimuli, while assertions consume real cache publications, HTTP outcomes, stale SDK-context refusal and process waits. Timeout observations are retained as timeout, not clean completion. A missing automatic retry remains a failing assertion. Notification waits observe the actual host RPC notification before a subsequent owner replacement can cancel it.

The launcher has a 900-second inner bound; the inherited Node launcher wrapper has a 600-second bound and may interrupt a cold-build plus five-minute qualification run before its inner bound. An interrupted run is not lifecycle qualification. Keep all receipts for the orchestrator; do not interpret fixture readiness/outer timeouts as runtime assertion failures.


The owning collector unit tests run with the ordinary status package checks. The nested adapter additionally needs build/vet/test with the reviewed SDK supplied through a disposable modfile. Neither this staging fixture nor its SDK prerequisite changes the selected source package or authorizes consumer activation.
